parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
The sketch graph for the titration of ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, with sodium hydroxide is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}
parts.text: In the region circled on the graph, identify the **two** organic species that are present in the solution. Explain why the pH of the mixture only changes slowly and gradually in this region when sodium hydroxide is being added.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The equivalence point in this acid-base titration is where the two solutions have been mixed in exactly equal molar proportion.

Suggest why the pH is greater than 7 at the equivalence point in this titration.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
An impure sample of ammonium vanadate(V), $\text{NH}_4\text{VO}_3$, with mass $0.150\text{ g}$, is dissolved in an excess of dilute acid.

In this solution all vanadium is present as $\text{VO}_2^+$ ions. An excess of zinc powder is added to the solution and all the $\text{VO}_2^+$ ions are reduced to $\text{V}^{2+}$ ions. The mixture is filtered to remove any remaining zinc powder.

$$\text{VO}_2^+ + 4\text{H}^+ + 3\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{V}^{2+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

When the resulting solution is titrated, $20.10\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.0250\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ oxidises all $\text{V}^{2+}$ ions back to $\text{VO}_2^+$ ions.

$$\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5\text{e}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Calculate the percentage by mass of $\text{NH}_4\text{VO}_3$ in the $0.150\text{ g}$ impure sample of $\text{NH}_4\text{VO}_3$.

Give your answer to three significant figures.

$[M_{\text{r}}\text{: } \text{NH}_4\text{VO}_3\text{, }116.9]$
